title: WPSB/16/2015 of Kanika Vs Uttarakhand Public Service Commission Haridwar

paras.text:
WPSB NO.16 OF 2015
Hon'ble V. K. Bist, J.
Hon'ble U. C. Dhyani, J.
Mr. Pankaj Tangwan, Advocate holding
brief of Mr. Anil K. Bisht, Advocate present for the
petitioner.
Mr. B. D. Kandpal, Advocate present for the
respondent.
By means of present writ petition, the
petitioner seeks to issue a direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding the respondent to treat her
candidature under the Scheduled Caste category,
inasmuch as, she belongs to the Chamar community
which has been notified as Scheduled Caste in the
State of Uttarakhand.
Brief facts of the case are that inadvertently,
the petitioner could not indicate her reserve category
in the first application form. Subsequently, for
abundant precaution, she had again submitted her
application form under the Scheduled Caste
category. Since the petitioner moved two
application forms, her candidature was rejected by
the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission
(hereinafter referred to as the Commission). Feeling
aggrieved, the petitioner filed a writ petition no.420
of 2014 (S/B) before the Division Bench of this
Court. Vide order dated 20.11.2014, the said writ
petition was disposed of with a direction that the first
application form of the petitioner be considered by
the Commission.
In the first application form, the petitioner has
applied under the General category. The
Commission considered the candidature of the
petitioner under the General category. Now, the
petitioner has approached this Court for a direction
to the respondents to treat her candidature under the
Scheduled Caste category. Since the petitioner has
not raised this plea in the earlier writ petition
no.420/2014 (S/B), which was filed against the
rejection of both the application forms, therefore, the
same cannot be made now.

Pursuant to the judgment and order dated
20.11.2014 passed in WPSS no.420/2014, the
Commission treated the petitioner under the General
category. Since the petitioner has applied under the
General category in the first application form, the
Commission was right in considering the petitioner
under the General category.
In such a situation, no direction can be issued.
The writ petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
 (U. C. Dhyani, J.) (V. K. Bist, J.)
Dated 13.01.2015
Rawat
